subject: Dedicated fleet prioritization: proposed gating and SLO trade-offs for Aurora
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@aurora.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Procurement <procurement@aurora.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing questions

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement needs confirmation on guaranteed GPU headroom during our first-quarter launch window (Nov–Dec). Our model needs sustained 700 tokens/sec at p95 and occasional spikes to 1,800 tokens/sec for short bursts. Can you confirm how Redwood would prioritize our reserved pool if overlapping demand arrives from other large customers? Also: any standard gating or escalation path if we see degradation?

I've attached a short requirement spreadsheet. Happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Sarah Li
Head of SRE, Aurora Therapeutics

Attachments: aurora_mlp_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@aurora.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the details and the sheet. We're confident we can meet the steady-state and burst profiles, but there are some policy choices we'll need to lock for it to be SLA-backed. Internally I've looped in Marissa (sales lead) and Vivek (product / capacity ops) to propose a concrete prioritization approach.

Proposed short summary (high level):
- Reserved pool: baseline guaranteed capacity sized to cover 750 tokens/sec sustained p95.
- Burst tranche: additional pooled burst capacity with throttles at 2x sustained rate; bursts are subject to global contention policies.
- Priority gating: tiered routing rule (1) reserved-only for committed customers during their hard window, (2) soft-reserve for near-committed customers with automated graceful degradation policies.

Before I respond to procurement I'd like an internal alignment on what we can promise vs what requires an exception (e.g., full preemption of other customers).

Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing questions

Thanks for pulling this together, Alex. A few points from sales/ops lens:

1) Deal priority level: Aurora is enterprise (high ACV) but they are in procurement. We should offer a "Committed Reserve + Burst" SKU but constrain absolute preemption. Full preemption would require a Reserved Priority Exception signed by the commercial leader.

2) Proposed gating (practical):
   - Hard window reservation: commit N GPUs during Aurora's launch window (time-bounded contract term).
   - Burst pool float: shared across customers; bursts hit fairness throttles at cluster-level.
   - Emergency preemption: 30-minute notification + 2x credit compensation if preemption occurs.

3) Sizing ask: product needs request workload traces (30 days) to recommend exact GPU count. If they can provide high-resolution logs we can convert to effective tokens/sec and map to our kernel-perf table.

I've attached a simple capacity tradeoff matrix (attached). Marissa

Attachments: capacity_tradeoff_matrix.csv (csv)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing questions

Quick technical readout:

We ran a back-of-envelope using Aurora's sheet and our 8-bit quantized perf profile. Findings:
- To cover sustained 750 tokens/sec p95 with 1.2s tail: ~6 A100-equivalent slots (low-latency config).
- To support bursts to 1,800 tokens/sec for short 2–5 minute windows: add 4 GPUs in a burst tranche.
- Risk: if multiple customers trigger burst windows simultaneously, the global batcher will serialize some requests leading to increased tail latency.

Operational recommendation:
- Offer Aurora a committed baseline of 6 GPUs + a managed burst tranche of 4 GPUs. Burst tranche backed by a soft-priority (best-effort) policy unless a Priority Exception is approved.
- For enterprise peace-of-mind, propose an SLA addendum: if Aurora experiences >10% p95 degradation for more than 30 consecutive minutes during their launch window, we trigger expedited mitigation (temporary capacity bump if available) and credits.

Action needed from leadership: do we approve Priority Exception language for this deal if Sales requests it? If no, we need to set clear client expectations around preemption and credits.

-Vivek
Senior Director, Capacity & Product
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing questions

Agree with Vivek's numbers. I want to raise one operational caveat: EdgeScale (a large early-stage customer with a year-long reserved pool) has a contractual right to 20% burst headroom during business hours for their product — if we approve Aurora's Priority Exception it will conflict with EdgeScale's current entitlement. We'll need:

- Approval from commercial leadership for any temporary override, and
- A short mutual-action plan that includes customer notification and a rollback path if EdgeScale's production is impacted.

If leadership is not comfortable with overrides, propose we communicate the managed-burst (soft priority) model to Aurora and offer a commercial credit-based "emergency bump" product that Aurora can buy to guarantee preemption for a limited window.

Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning
